surface: the 69 numeric levers of src/fabric/levers.py::FABLevers, driven at nan / inf / -inf / 0
how_it_was_driven: One FRESH SUBPROCESS per cell (277 processes: 276 cells + one baseline). Each cell calls spine.lever._reopen_assembly() and spine.rng.reset_issued(), then a real spine.assemble.build() over a DICT environment (never os.environ) carrying BASE={RUN_SEED:7, RUN_DEVICE:cpu, FAB_N0:6, FAB_SLOTS:12, FAB_CHAIN_K:3, FAB_DEPTH0:3, FAB_HOPS:4} plus the one swept PREFIX_FIELD; then src/fabric/api.py::build(d_model=16, signature_dim=12, device=cpu, generator=rng.rng_for('fabric',1234)); then src/fabric/api.py::forward TWICE (step_windows=1 and 2, training=True, head+targets supplied) with a seeded draw; then the composed objective spine/compose.py backwards -- cross_entropy(logits) + aux_loss -- and torch.autograd.grad over both adapter banks, halt_b, every shared module, the head and the incoming representation; then src/fabric/api.py::manage_period. Every gate line, the whole Population.counters ledger and the finiteness of every tensor were recorded and diffed against the baseline. BASE was chosen so the mechanisms are live rather than dormant: at these widths fab.explore, fab.discover, fab.distinctness, fab.balance, fab.halt, fab.identity_round_trip and a 3-hop walk all FIRE on the baseline. FAB.observe, FAB.manage, FAB.grow_check, FAB.own_lr_scale, FAB.counters, FAB.state_dict and FAB.load_state_dict were each called once and each raised NotImplementedError -- they are P4 stubs, which is what makes 33 of the 69 levers UNREACHABLE_TODAY rather than inert.

findings.detail: src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce resolves an int lever as `v = int(float(raw))` inside a `try` that catches only `(TypeError, ValueError)`. int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, which is NOT caught, so it walks straight out of coerce -> from_env -> spine/assemble.py::build as a bare `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer` naming no lever, no value and no package. The SAME line at 'nan' raises ValueError, IS caught, and becomes the correct LeverError -- so one function refuses one spelling by name and the other by a stack trace. This is not fabric's defect: it is the single reader, and every int lever in all thirteen packages is behind it. Widening the except clause to include OverflowError is a one-token repair that converts 52 of this sweep's cells (and the equivalent in every other package) from REFUSED_BADLY to REFUSED_BY_NAME.
findings.repro:
FAB_GRACE=inf: OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
  at src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce -> `elif isinstance(d, int):    v = int(float(raw))`
FAB_GRACE=nan: LeverError: FAB_GRACE='nan' is not a int    <- the same line, refused by name

findings.detail: FAB_PRESSURE is a FLOAT lever, so coerce accepts all three. It is then consumed during spine/assemble.py::build by the FAB.d_operating_population coupling, which calls spine/derive.py::operating_population -- whose `n = int(exact)` raises a bare ValueError at nan and a bare OverflowError at +/-inf. The operator sees a numeric error out of a derive function with no mention of FAB_PRESSURE, of the coupling, or of the fact that a fraction was typed as a non-number. It is the one float lever in this package whose bad value is caught at all, and it is caught by accident.
findings.repro:
FAB_PRESSURE=nan -> ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer   (stage: spine.assemble.build)
FAB_PRESSURE=inf -> OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
FAB_PRESSURE=-inf -> OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer

findings.detail: FAB_ALPHA is the residual mixing coefficient of one fabric step, `h = norm(h + alive*(alpha*(mixture-h)))`, multiplied UNGUARDED in src/fabric/api.py::forward. It is NOT one of the eleven magnitude levers src/fabric/api.py::build refuses -- build's own comment names FAB_ALPHA in the list it deliberately does not touch. All three values assemble with no warning, FAB.build accepts them, and one forward pass makes aux_loss nan, the composed objective nan, 19 of 23 gradient-carrying tensors non-finite, and -- because the centroid EMA writes back inside the same pass -- pop.cent PERMANENTLY non-finite, so the population is destroyed even if the lever were corrected mid-run. The fab.halt gate meanwhile prints the verdict FIRED over a mass it reads as nan. This is the FAB_BALANCE=nan defect the sweep was commissioned for, in a lever the FAB_BALANCE repair explicitly excluded.

FAB_ALPHA=nan   aux=nan            composed=nan            non-finite grads 19/23  cent finite=False
FAB_ALPHA=inf   aux=nan            composed=nan            non-finite grads 19/23  cent finite=False

findings.detail: The centroid EMA rate is multiplied unguarded in src/fabric/api.py::_ground_update and written back into pop.cent, the routing centroid BUFFER. All three values make pop.cent non-finite on the first pass; every routing logit is then nan, aux_loss is nan, the composed objective is nan and 19/23 gradients are non-finite. The report is worse than the number: the fab.discover gate prints `armed, did not fire (0 handover(s), 0 distinct recipient(s) vs cosine distance > 0.35)` -- 'the discovery mechanism ran and found nothing' -- for the pass that just poisoned every centroid it touched. That is a gate stating a verdict that is false about its own subject.

findings.detail: The halt-mass ceiling reaches `ph = raw.clamp(max=halt_max)` in src/fabric/api.py::forward. clamp(max=nan) returns nan and clamp(max=-inf) returns -inf, so the halted mass -- which multiplies the residual (`alive = alive * (1 - ph)`) and the per-hop vote -- becomes non-finite and takes aux, the composed objective, 19/23 gradients and pop.cent with it. FAB_HALT_MAX is one of the eight levers build's comment lists as deliberately NOT range-checked ('a range ruling this body has not measured'); this is the measurement. Note the gate renders its own poison honestly -- 'mean halted mass nan vs halt_max=nan' -- which is the only reason this is visible at all.

  Gate fab.halt: FIRED (mean halted mass nan vs halt_max=nan)
FAB_HALT_MAX=-inf  aux=nan composed=nan non-finite grads 19/23 cent finite=False
  Gate fab.halt: FIRED (mean halted mass nan vs halt_max=-inf); fab.halt_clamped=2

findings.detail: src/fabric/api.py::_decay_to_floor returns `max(floor, 1.0 - step_n/max(1, warm_n))`. Python's max keeps its FIRST argument when the comparison is False, and `x > nan` is always False -- so max(nan, 0.9998) is nan. The balance scale is then nan, `aux = aux + balance_w * bal_scale * bal` is nan, and 17 of 23 gradients are non-finite. At +inf the scale is inf and aux is inf, with the same 17 non-finite gradients. In both cases the fab.balance gate prints FIRED and renders the poison as the arithmetic that justified it. FAB_BAL_FLOOR is the third of the levers build's comment names as untouched.
findings.repro:
FAB_BAL_FLOOR=nan  aux=nan  composed=nan  non-finite grads 17/23
  Gate fab.balance: FIRED (balance=0.01 x warm=nan vs > 0)
FAB_BAL_FLOOR=inf  aux=inf  composed=inf  non-finite grads 17/23
  Gate fab.balance: FIRED (balance=0.01 x warm=inf vs > 0)

findings.detail: This one is INVISIBLE at step 0 and arrives later, which is why a same-window sweep alone would miss it. max(-inf, 1 - step/bal_warm) is just `1 - step/bal_warm`, so with the floor removed the load-balance scale goes NEGATIVE the moment step exceeds bal_warm (4000 windows by default) and keeps growing without bound. Measured at step_windows=100000 with bal_warm at its default: the scale is -24.0, aux_loss is -0.196 against +0.497 at the shipped floor, and the composed objective drops from 2.992 to 2.299 -- the load-balance term applied with its sign REVERSED and 160x the intended magnitude, i.e. the objective now PAYS the population to collapse onto one expert. That is bit-for-bit the harm src/fabric/api.py::build refuses FAB_BALANCE<0 for, reached through the lever the same comment declines to check. The gate reports it as a firing: 'FIRED (balance=0.01 x warm=-24.0 vs > 0)'. Hostile to goal B at its root.

step=100000 FAB_BAL_FLOOR=0.15  aux=0.4970445930957794  composed=2.9919025897979736
  Gate fab.balance: FIRED (balance=0.01 x warm=0.15 vs > 0)
step=100000 FAB_BAL_FLOOR=-inf  aux=-0.19620820879936218 composed=2.298649787902832
  Gate fab.balance: FIRED (balance=0.01 x warm=-24.0 vs > 0)
(at step_windows=1 the -inf cell is bit-identical to the baseline: aux 0.5120277404785156)

findings.detail: FAB_RANK=0 assembles with no warning and FAB.build allocates A as (cap, d_model, 0) and B as (cap, 0, d_model) -- every expert has ZERO parameters and dW = A@B is identically zero for the life of the run, so the entire population is a no-op that the optimizer still holds. Worse, the identity embedder's input is 2*d_model*rank = 0 numbers, so eemb(weights) is the same constant for every expert, src/fabric/api.py::_var_cov divides by a zero variance and aux_loss comes back nan -- the composed objective the composition root backwards is nan. The three geometry levers are compared against the built pool at the top of forward, and 0 passes that check because the pool was built at 0 too.
findings.repro:
FAB_RANK=0  aux=nan  composed=nan  A.shape=[12, 16, 0]  n_live=6  sum|g|max over every parameter = 35713.02
(baseline: aux=0.5120277404785156 composed=3.0068857669830322 A.shape=[12, 16, 8] sum|g|max = 1.2194)

findings.detail: FAB_DK is the width of the routing identity space. At 0 every per-expert key, the router's query and the halt key are zero-width vectors: `keys @ q` is a sum over nothing, the spawn test reads gap=1.0 and typ=1.0 for every query on every pass (the manufactured 'infinitely novel' reading _spawn_check's docstring exists to avoid), and aux_loss comes back nan, so the composed objective is nan. Routing identity -- the premise of the whole identity design -- is silently deleted and the run trains on a nan loss.
findings.repro:
FAB_DK=0  aux=nan  composed=nan  n_live=6
  Gate fab.spawn: armed, did not fire (gap=1.0 vs max(2.0*typ=1.0, floor=0.02))    <- typ=1.0 is manufactured
(baseline: gap=0.85165, typ=0.797899, aux=0.5120277404785156)

findings.detail: The identity embedder's hidden width. At 0 eemb is Linear(2*d*r -> 0) followed by Linear(0 -> dk), so its output is a CONSTANT that does not depend on the expert's weights at all: every expert embeds to one point. That is the collapsed identity space src/fabric/api.py::_var_cov and the emb_var term exist to detect and prevent, arriving as a geometry the operator typed rather than as a training failure -- and it is arrived at silently: aux_loss is finite (0.5377) and every gate still prints FIRED, so nothing in the report says the identity channel is dead. The sum of |grad|max over every parameter explodes from 1.22 to 127745.
findings.repro:
FAB_EMB_HID=0  aux=0.5376548171043396  composed=3.032512903213501  sum|g|max = 127745.086
  Gate fab.identity_round_trip: FIRED (ae_w=0.5, emb_var=1.0, 6 embedding(s) scored ...)
  Gate fab.spawn: armed, did not fire (gap=1.0 vs max(2.0*typ=1.0, floor=0.02))
(baseline: sum|g|max = 1.2194051730269422, gap=0.85165, typ=0.797899)

findings.detail: src/fabric/api.py::_spawn_check decides with `if gap < max(float(spawn_mult) * typ, float(spawn_floor))`. max(nan, 0.02) is nan (Python keeps the first argument because `0.02 > nan` is False), and `gap < nan` is False -- so the test SPAWNS UNCONDITIONALLY, on every query, for the life of the run, and spawn_floor -- the absolute floor whose declared purpose is 'so a degenerate population cannot spawn on every query' -- is bypassed entirely. Measured: two forward passes, two spawns, n_live 6 -> 8, fab.spawn_declined 0. The population runs to pop.cap; growth never reallocates, so the run then holds a pool full of specification-decoded experts nobody asked for. The gate renders a threshold that was never used: 'max(nan*typ=0.71431, floor=0.02)' reads as though 0.71431 or 0.02 governed the comparison.
findings.repro:
FAB_SPAWN_MULT=2.0   n_live after 2 passes=6  spawned=0 declined=2 | Gate fab.spawn: armed, did not fire (gap=0.85165 vs max(2.0*typ=0.797899, floor=0.02))
FAB_SPAWN_MULT=nan   n_live after 2 passes=8  spawned=2 declined=0 | Gate fab.spawn: FIRED (gap=0.85165 vs max(nan*typ=0.71431, floor=0.02))

findings.detail: src/fabric/api.py::_entry_logits and ::_halt_logit both divide by `temp = max(1e-3, route_t)`. At +inf every routing logit and the halt logit become exactly 0.0, so the softmax over the population is UNIFORM: there is no routing decision left, the region cosine and the learned identity term are both erased, and both project goals run through the mechanism that just stopped existing. Nothing says so -- Gate fab.route_learned still prints 'FIRED (route_learn=True vs route_learn=True)', and the only visible symptom is that both batch rows select the identical experts and the halt mass jumps to its uniform value.
findings.repro:
FAB_ROUTE_T=0.1  aux=0.5120277404785156 expert_ids=[[0, 5], [2, 0]] halt_mass=0.168269 | Gate fab.route_learned: FIRED (route_learn=True vs route_learn=True)
FAB_ROUTE_T=inf  aux=0.4987477958202362 expert_ids=[[3, 5], [3, 5]] halt_mass=0.370262 | Gate fab.route_learned: FIRED (route_learn=True vs route_learn=True)

findings.detail: The mirror of FAB_SPAWN_MULT=nan and quieter. max(spawn_mult*typ, nan) returns spawn_mult*typ, so the ABSOLUTE FLOOR IS SILENTLY DELETED while the gate prints 'floor=nan' as though it were in force. On a healthy population the relative term dominates and nothing changes -- measured bit-identical to the baseline here. The harm is exactly the case the lever exists for: when the identity space has collapsed, typ -> 0, the threshold goes to 0 and the population spawns on every query with no floor to stop it. FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=+inf is the opposite and also silent: the threshold is inf, spawn can never fire again, and the gate reports 'armed, did not fire' -- the armed-but-0 state standing in for UNREACHABLE, which spine/gate.py exists to forbid.

FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=0.02  n_live=6 spawned=0 | Gate fab.spawn: armed, did not fire (gap=0.85165 vs max(2.0*typ=0.797899, floor=0.02))
FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=nan   n_live=6 spawned=0 | Gate fab.spawn: armed, did not fire (gap=0.85165 vs max(2.0*typ=0.797899, floor=nan))

findings.detail: This is the three-answers-for-one-number defect that src/fabric/api.py::manage_period and spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows were both repaired for at NEGATIVE values, still live at zero. flush_period_windows refuses `period_windows.n < 0` and only that, so 0 falls through to the floor and FAB.d_manage_period resolves to Flushes(1) -- 'manage on EVERY flush', the tightest cadence in the system, computed at build time through the declared coupling table. Meanwhile FAB.manage_period(fab) returns Windows(0) and spine/derive.py::cadences_that_cannot_fire reports ('fab.manage', 0, 0), i.e. 'this gate cannot fire' -- and that function's own comment calls a period of zero A SENTINEL. Two live readers, opposite sentences, one lever, no warning. The behaviour is latent only because RUN.Cadences.due is a P4 stub; the WIRE is live today.

findings.detail: Bit-identical to the default on the measured pass, and that is the finding: the ceiling is silently REMOVED. fabric/levers.py::FABLevers.halt_max declares it 'A BARRIER, NOT A PREFERENCE ... at halt=1 the experts receive no gradient at all, and an expert that receives no gradient can never become worth routing to: an absorbing state.' At +inf raw.clamp(max=inf) is the identity, so the halt operator may take the entire routing mass and the population can be starved of gradient permanently. Nothing refuses it and the gate simply prints 'halt_max=inf'. Low because nothing differs on a short pass; the class is 'a cap that does not cap'.

FAB_HALT_MAX=inf  aux=0.5120277404785156  composed=3.0068857669830322  non-finite grads 0/23  cent finite=True
  Gate fab.halt: FIRED (mean halted mass 0.1683 vs halt_max=inf)
(baseline: aux=0.5120277404785156 composed=3.0068857669830322 -- bit-identical)

findings.detail: cap = max(n0, slots) is the declared arithmetic, so slots=0 legitimately yields cap = n0 and FAB.build is right to accept it. What is not right is the setpoint it derives: spine/derive.py::operating_population carries `n = max(3, n)` -- its own docstring says 'the same floor as the gate's n_live <= 2' -- and then returns `min(n_slots, n) if n_slots >= 3 else n_slots`, which BYPASSES that floor entirely at slots<3. FAB_SLOTS=0 therefore prints fab.operating_population=0: the utilization cull's setpoint is zero, so the cull gate is open from step 0 against the whole population, and the number the run reports as its own operating size is a number the floor above it was written to make impossible.
findings.repro:
FAB_SLOTS=0   fab.cap=6  fab.operating_population=0   A.shape=[6, 16, 8]  warnings=[]
  Gate fab.spawn: UNREACHABLE (not measured vs max(2.0*typ, floor=0.02)) -- the pool is full at cap=6 ...
(baseline FAB_SLOTS=12: fab.cap=12  fab.operating_population=6)

findings.detail: `depth = max(1, min(int(pop.depth_now), hops, 2 + n//2))` in src/fabric/api.py::forward, so a maximum hop budget of ZERO silently yields ONE hop -- a cap that does not cap. The gate then prints a reason that is false about the configuration it is describing: 'FAB_DEPTH0 >= FAB_HOPS: the chain already starts at the budget', when the budget is 0, depth0 is 3, and the walk actually took 1. The number and the sentence disagree in the same rendered line.
findings.repro:
FAB_HOPS=0:
  Gate fab.depth_curriculum: armed, did not fire (depth0=3 vs hops=0) -- FAB_DEPTH0 >= FAB_HOPS: the chain already starts at the budget.
  Gate fab.forward.routed: FIRED (1 hop(s) over 6 experts vs depth=1)

findings.detail: src/fabric/api.py::build ACCEPTS n0=0, allocates the full pool at cap=max(0, slots) and founds a population of nobody. The refusal comes one entry point later, from FAB.forward, as a bare ValueError. The message is a good one and it does mention n0 in prose, but it is not a LeverError, it does not name FAB_N0 or the value the operator typed, and it fires after a Population, its two adapter banks and seven shared modules have already been allocated -- so the operator gets a runtime error on the first routed window rather than a startup refusal. build already reads n0 to compute cap; the check belongs there.
findings.repro:
FAB_N0=0 -> stage fab.build: OK (Population built, cap=12, n_live=0)
         -> stage fab.forward: ValueError: FAB.forward: n_live is 0. An empty population is not a routing outcome; fabric/api.py::build founds n0 experts and nothing may reduce it to none.

This is LATENT, NOT ABSENT: nothing in coerce, in the Lever declaration or in FAB refuses a non-finite float, so each of these arms the moment P4 writes the body, and the bodies they arm are the cull, the failure tolerance, the mutation scale, the merge distance and the per-expert learning rate -- i.e. selection and the optimizer, where a NaN is a silently deleted population rather than a nan loss. One of them already crosses a package boundary today: FAB_COMP_EMA=nan is carried by the declared coupling into DOM's frozen Config as DOM.d_comp_ema=nan with no warning, waiting for DOM.note_competence (also a stub) to read it.

findings.detail: dom_min is declared as 'the floor that stops int(0.10 * small_n) collapsing to zero and banning every expert from every domain it does not already hold'. Set to 0 the floor is gone and src/fabric/api.py::_breadth_ban computes limit=0, at which `len(pop.dom_of[e]) >= 0` is true for EVERY expert, so the breadth cap would mask the entire population out of routing -- caught only incidentally by the `if int(ban.sum()) < n` guard, which then switches the cap off completely rather than reporting it. Unreachable today for the reason the gate itself gives: FAB.observe is the only writer of dom_of and it is a stub, so no expert holds an affiliation and the comparison never runs. It arms with P4.

summary: 69 numeric levers enumerated from src/fabric/levers.py::FABLevers (26 int, 43 float; the estimate was ~69), driven at nan / inf / -inf / 0 = 276 cells, each in a fresh subprocess through a real spine.assemble.build() over a dict environment, then FAB.build, then two FAB.forward passes, the composed objective, torch.autograd.grad over every gradient-carrying tensor, and FAB.manage_period. OUTCOMES: UNREACHABLE_TODAY 103, REFUSED_BY_NAME 59, REFUSED_BADLY 56, ACCEPTED_HARMFUL 26, ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE 25, ACCEPTED_INERT 7, CRASHED 0. THE HEADLINE: the FAB_BALANCE=nan defect is not closed, it is relocated. build() now refuses eleven magnitude levers at nan/+inf, and the same comment that adds that refusal LISTS the levers it declines to check -- FAB_ALPHA, FAB_ROUTE_T, FAB_HALT_MAX, FAB_BAL_FLOOR, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR, FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W. Five of those six carry the identical defect: FAB_ALPHA, FAB_CENT_EMA, FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W, FAB_HALT_MAX and FAB_BAL_FLOOR each take one forward pass to make aux_loss nan, the composed objective nan and 17-19 of 23 gradient-carrying tensors non-finite, and the first four also write NaN permanently into pop.cent, so the population cannot be recovered by fixing the lever. Twelve cells, all critical, all silent. THREE MORE CLASSES the sweep found that a value-range rule alone would miss: (1) the ZERO of three GEOMETRY levers -- FAB_RANK=0 builds experts with no parameters and a nan loss, FAB_DK=0 deletes routing identity and returns a nan loss, FAB_EMB_HID=0 collapses every expert's identity to one point and explodes sum|g|max from 1.22 to 127745 -- none refused, none reported; (2) MAX AND FLOOR GUARDS THAT NaN WALKS THROUGH, because Python's max/min keep their first argument when the comparison is False: FAB_SPAWN_MULT=nan spawns an expert on EVERY query (measured n_live 6->8 in two passes) and bypasses the absolute floor entirely, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=nan silently deletes the floor while the gate prints 'floor=nan', and FAB_ROUTE_T=inf turns every routing logit into 0.0 so the population is routed UNIFORMLY while Gate fab.route_learned still prints FIRED; (3) a LATE-ARRIVING SIGN INVERSION -- FAB_BAL_FLOOR=-inf is bit-identical to the baseline at step_windows=1 and, at step_windows=100000, drives the load-balance scale to -24.0, making aux_loss NEGATIVE (-0.196 against +0.497) and paying the objective to collapse the population onto one expert, which is exactly the harm FAB_BALANCE<0 is refused for. ONE SPINE-WIDE DEFECT, worth more than any single fabric lever: src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce resolves int levers as int(float(raw)) inside a try that catches only (TypeError, ValueError). int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, uncaught -- so all 26 int levers at +/-inf (52 of this sweep's cells, and the same in every other package) fail with a bare 'OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer' naming nothing, while the SAME LINE at 'nan' raises ValueError, is caught, and produces the correct LeverError. One token in one except clause fixes half of the REFUSED_BADLY column tree-wide. WHAT THE SWEEP DID NOT FIND, which matters for the ruling: 33 of the 69 levers (23 float + 10 int) have NO live reader at all -- FAB.observe, FAB.manage, FAB.grow_check, FAB.own_lr_scale, FAB.counters, FAB.state_dict and FAB.load_state_dict were each called and each raised NotImplementedError. Their nan and inf values freeze into the Config, one already crosses a package boundary (DOM.d_comp_ema=nan, silently), and all of them arm the day P4 lands, in the cull, the mutation scale and the per-expert learning rate. That is 103 UNREACHABLE_TODAY cells that are latent, not absent. FOR THE CENTRAL-VS-PER-PACKAGE RULING: a blanket 'no nan, no inf' rule in spine/lever.py would refuse exactly ZERO of the 25 legitimate specials found here -- every declared sentinel in this package is a ZERO, not an infinity (depth0=0 no curriculum, dom_frac=0 cap off, ec_w/hop_sup/rescue=0 off, route_region_w=0 predicted-weights-only, plus the guard-floored chain_k/ens_k/ind_k/emb_every/route_t/bal_warm/ponder_warm zeros). No FAB lever uses +inf to mean 'no cap'; the three that come closest (halt_max, spawn_floor, spawn_mult) all BREAK at inf rather than meaning anything by it. The only values a central refusal would take away are three that are provably identical to an already-legal zero (FAB_ROUTE_T=nan/-inf, FAB_SPAWN_MULT=-inf, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=-inf), so nothing an operator can ask for is lost. What a central rule CANNOT do is the other half of this report: the zeros of FAB_RANK, FAB_DK, FAB_EMB_HID, FAB_N0, FAB_SLOTS, FAB_HOPS and FAB_MANAGE_EVERY are all finite, all legal to a type check, and all defects -- those need FAB's own refusal at build(), and FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0 needs spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows to refuse `< 1` where it today refuses only `< 0`.
